memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The elders of Israel will listen to you. Then you and the elders are to go to the king of Egypt and say to him, 'The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord our God.' But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless a mighty hand compels him." - Exodus 3:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God sends Moses with a clear instruction — and with a clear warning. He tells him in advance: Pharaoh will refuse.

Think about that. God did not send Moses in with false optimism. He did not promise quick success. He said, this is going to be hard, and it will take My mighty hand before anything moves.

We often assume that if something is God's will, it will go smoothly. That assumption has crushed a lot of believers. Opposition is not proof that you have misheard God. Sometimes it is exactly what He predicted.

Jesus was equally honest with His followers. In this world you will have trouble, He said — and then added, but take heart, I have overcome the world (Jn 16:33). He never recruited anyone under false advertising.

Obey God with your eyes open. Expect resistance. And expect God's mighty hand.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I assumed that difficulty means I am outside God's will?
2. Am I prepared to keep obeying when the first attempt fails?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when obedience meets resistance, keep me steady. Help me to trust Your mighty hand rather than easy results. Amen.
